title: The Heart Structure
content:
# The Heart Structure

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe the external and internal structure of the heart
- Identify the four chambers and major blood vessels
- Explain the functions of heart valves
- Describe the blood flow through the heart

## Introduction

The **heart** is a muscular organ that pumps blood around the body. It beats continuously throughout life - about 100,000 times per day. Understanding its structure helps explain how it efficiently pumps blood through two separate circuits simultaneously.

## Key Concepts

### Overview of the Heart

**Basic facts:**
- Size: About the size of your fist
- Weight: ~300g in adults
- Location: Centre of chest, between lungs
- Made of: Cardiac muscle
- Surrounded by: Pericardium (protective membrane)

### External Structure

**Features visible from outside:**
- Coronary arteries (supply heart muscle)
- Coronary veins (drain heart muscle)
- Major vessels entering and leaving
- Fatty tissue on surface
- Pericardium surrounding heart

[DIAGRAM: External view of heart showing coronary vessels]

### Internal Structure

**Four chambers:**

| Chamber | Location | Function |
|---------|----------|----------|
| Right atrium | Upper right | Receives deoxygenated blood from body |
| Right ventricle | Lower right | Pumps blood to lungs |
| Left atrium | Upper left | Receives oxygenated blood from lungs |
| Left ventricle | Lower left | Pumps blood to body |

[DIAGRAM: Cross-section of heart with all parts labelled]

### The Septum

**Septum:**
- Wall dividing left and right sides
- Prevents mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood
- Made of muscle and connective tissue

**"Hole in the heart":**
- Defect in septum
- Blood mixes between sides
- Can cause health problems

### Heart Valves

**Four valves:**

| Valve | Location | Prevents backflow from |
|-------|----------|----------------------|
| Tricuspid | Between right atrium and ventricle | Ventricle to atrium |
| Bicuspid (mitral) | Between left atrium and ventricle | Ventricle to atrium |
| Pulmonary | Between right ventricle and pulmonary artery | Artery to ventricle |
| Aortic | Between left ventricle and aorta | Artery to ventricle |

**Function of valves:**
- Ensure one-way flow
- Open when pressure behind is greater
- Close when pressure in front is greater
- Heart sounds ("lub-dub") are valves closing

[DIAGRAM: Heart valves in open and closed positions]

### Atrioventricular Valves

**Tricuspid and bicuspid valves:**
- Between atria and ventricles
- Have flaps (cusps) of tissue
- Attached to tendons (chordae tendineae)
- Tendons attached to papillary muscles
- Prevent valves inverting during contraction

### Semilunar Valves

**Pulmonary and aortic valves:**
- Pocket-like flaps
- Three cusps each
- Fill with blood and close when blood pushes back
- No tendons needed

### Major Blood Vessels

**Entering the heart:**

| Vessel | Enters | Carries |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Vena cava (superior and inferior) | Right atrium | Deoxygenated blood from body |
| Pulmonary vein | Left atrium | Oxygenated blood from lungs |

**Leaving the heart:**

| Vessel | Leaves | Carries |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Pulmonary artery | Right ventricle | Deoxygenated blood to lungs |
| Aorta | Left ventricle | Oxygenated blood to body |

### Wall Thickness

**Different thicknesses:**

| Part | Wall thickness | Reason |
|------|---------------|--------|
| Atria | Thin | Only pump blood to ventricles (short distance) |
| Right ventricle | Medium | Pumps to lungs (short distance) |
| Left ventricle | Thick | Pumps to whole body (long distance, high pressure) |

**Left ventricle wall is 2-3 times thicker than right ventricle.**

### Blood Flow Through the Heart

**Step by step:**

1. Deoxygenated blood enters **right atrium** via **vena cava**
2. Blood flows through **tricuspid valve** to **right ventricle**
3. Right ventricle contracts, blood goes through **pulmonary valve**
4. Blood travels to lungs via **pulmonary artery**
5. Oxygenated blood returns via **pulmonary vein** to **left atrium**
6. Blood flows through **bicuspid valve** to **left ventricle**
7. Left ventricle contracts, blood goes through **aortic valve**
8. Blood travels to body via **aorta**

### Coronary Circulation

**Heart muscle needs its own blood supply:**

| Vessel | Function |
|--------|----------|
| Coronary arteries | Supply oxygen and nutrients to heart muscle |
| Coronary veins | Remove waste from heart muscle |

**Coronary arteries branch from aorta** just above aortic valve.

**Blockage of coronary arteries:**
- Causes heart attack (myocardial infarction)
- Heart muscle dies without oxygen
- Can be fatal

### Cardiac Muscle

**Special properties:**
- Myogenic (generates own contractions)
- Doesn't fatigue (works continuously)
- Interconnected cells
- Rich in mitochondria (lots of ATP needed)
- Rich blood supply

### How to Remember Blood Flow

**Mnemonic for vessels:**
- Arteries carry blood **A**way from heart
- Veins carry blood **to** heart (V points towards)

**For pulmonary vessels:**
- Pulmonary artery = deoxygenated (opposite to usual)
- Pulmonary vein = oxygenated (opposite to usual)

## Common Exam Questions

- Label a diagram of the heart
- Describe the flow of blood through the heart
- Explain why the left ventricle wall is thicker
- Describe the function of heart valves

## Common Misconceptions

- **Misconception:** The heart has two sides doing the same job
- **Reality:** Right side pumps to lungs; left side pumps to body

- **Misconception:** Valves actively open and close
- **Reality:** Valves open and close passively due to pressure differences

- **Misconception:** All arteries carry oxygenated blood
- **Reality:** Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood

- **Misconception:** The heart is on the left side of the chest
- **Reality:** It's in the centre, tilted slightly left

## Practice Questions

1. Name the valve between the left atrium and left ventricle. (1 mark)

2. State which chamber of the heart has the thickest wall and explain why. (2 marks)

3. Describe the function of heart valves. (2 marks)

4. Describe the path of blood from the vena cava to the aorta. Name all chambers and valves. (4 marks)

5. Explain why the heart needs its own blood supply. (2 marks)

6. A person has a 'hole in the heart' between the two ventricles. Explain the consequences this might have for their blood. (4 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Atrium | Upper chamber that receives blood |
| Ventricle | Lower chamber that pumps blood out |
| Septum | Wall between left and right sides |
| Valve | Structure preventing backflow |
| Tricuspid valve | Valve between right atrium and ventricle |
| Bicuspid valve | Valve between left atrium and ventricle |
| Aorta | Main artery leaving left ventricle |
| Vena cava | Main vein entering right atrium |
| Coronary | Relating to heart's own blood supply |

## Summary

- Heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles
- Septum separates left and right sides
- Four valves ensure one-way blood flow
- Right side pumps deoxygenated blood to lungs
- Left side pumps oxygenated blood to body
- Left ventricle has thickest wall (pumps furthest)
- Coronary arteries supply heart muscle
- Valves open and close based on pressure differences
